data.title: Buy Maintained Despite Near-Term Pressure as FY27 EBITDA Recovery Supports Outlook; Price Target Trimmed to $80
data.description:
Reinhardt van der Walt, an analyst from Bank of America Securities, reiterated the Buy rating on ArcelorMittal. The associated price target was lowered to €80.00.

Reinhardt van der Walt gave his rating based on several factors, led by a constructive FY27 outlook despite near-term pressure. Q3 EBITDA modestly exceeded consensus, indicating greater resilience than investors feared, while management said earlier steel-price increases should begin offsetting elevated costs in Q1 FY27. Higher prices, annual automotive contract resets, and improving volumes are expected to drive a strong margin recovery and support more than $12 billion in FY27 EBITDA.

Although Q4 should still reflect price-cost delays, destocking, and high European energy costs, the analyst views it as a temporary clearing period rather than a deterioration in the long-term thesis. North American pricing gains and stronger exports provide support, while seasonal mining volumes add potential; despite mixed segment risks, the Buy remains attractive with the official $80 price objective revised down from $81 and substantial upside to the EUR55.12 share price.

In another report released today, Deutsche Bank also maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a €70.00 price target.

0RP9’s price has also changed slightly for the past six months – from EUR49.580 to EUR54.500, which is a 9.92% increase.

data.title: BETA’s $37 Price Target Unchanged as Component Growth and Certification Progress Support Outlook
data.description:
Bank of America Securities analyst Ronald Epstein reiterated a Buy rating on BETA Technologies, Inc. Class A today and set a price target of $37.00.

Ronald Epstein’s rating is based on several factors, including BETA’s progress toward aircraft certification and its broader position in electric and hybrid aviation. He sees value in the company’s mix of VTOL and CTOL aircraft, charging infrastructure, and aviation components, which gives it exposure beyond the eVTOL market. The unchanged $37 price target reflects confidence that recent quarterly results and improved guidance support this strategy.
Epstein is also encouraged by the strong expansion of component sales, which delivered substantial year-over-year growth and improved margins while representing a meaningful portion of BETA’s backlog. He views the slower aircraft build rate as a deliberate use of capital rather than a fundamental setback, since constrained production capacity helps limit costly inventory and rework before certification. In addition, expanding pilot programs, FAA authorization for customer demonstrations, and the expected transition to revenue-generating flights provide additional catalysts for growth.

In another report released today, Morgan Stanley also maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a $33.00 price target.
